node.title: Re: Problems learning WebDAV with dav_this and HTTP::DAV
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
The trace on this is:

  • The 400 Bad Request is generated at [https://metacpan.org/source/CPANEL/Net-DAV-Server-1.305/lib/Net/DAV/Server.pm#L84|Net::DAV::Server line 84],
  • caused by the call to the propfind method, which fails at [https://metacpan.org/source/CPANEL/Net-DAV-Server-1.305/lib/Net/DAV/Server.pm#L821|Net::DAV::Server line 821],
  • which calls Net::DAV::LockManager's list_all_locks,
  • which fails due to the "Not a valid user name" error at [https://metacpan.org/source/CPANEL/Net-DAV-Server-1.305/lib/Net/DAV/LockManager.pm#L221|Net::DAV::LockManager line 221].

The difference between e.g. Nautilus and [mod://HTTP::DAV] is that the former sends a ... request, while the latter sends a ... request, which hits the above branch of code. There, the propfind method attempts to [https://metacpan.org/source/CPANEL/Net-DAV-Server-1.305/lib/Net/DAV/Server.pm#L820|use] the HTTP Basic Auth user credentials, which it doesn't have because AFAICT it never requests them from the client (Update: and at the moment I don't see a way to force the client to send the auth, although I may be missing something).

Unfortunately, that's where my analysis ends for now - I don't know much about WebDAV and I'm not sure which module is at fault here, although I suspect it's [mod://Net::DAV::Server] not handling this type of request, because the [mod://HTTP::DAV] client code seems to work fine for me on two different servers. So you might just want to use a different server for testing, and perhaps file a bug for [mod://Net::DAV::Server] (although that module hasn't been updated since 2013).

I like to sometimes use [https://www.lighttpd.net/|lighttpd] for quick & dirty test servers. On Ubuntu, sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends lighttpd lighttpd-mod-webdav, sudo systemctl stop lighttpd, and sudo systemctl disable lighttpd (assuming you don't want it running all the time), then create a file /tmp/lhttpd.conf with the following contents ([https://redmine.lighttpd.net/projects/lighttpd/wiki/Docs_ModWebDAV|module docs]):

server.document-root = "/tmp/foo/" server.port = 4242 server.bind = "127.0.0.1" server.modules += ( "mod_webdav" ) $HTTP["url"] =~ "^/dav($|/)" { webdav.activate = "enable" #webdav.is-readonly = "disable" # (default) webdav.sqlite-db-name = "/tmp/foo_webdav.db" }

Then run mkdir -p /tmp/foo/dav and lighttpd -Df /tmp/lhttpd.conf, and you can then access the server using [mod://HTTP::DAV] at http://localhost:4242/dav/.

There are lots of other modules available, see the files (including the README) that get installed at /etc/lighttpd/conf-available, it includes SSL, authentication, CGI, and FastCGI.
